_page: The public homepage of Artosia at artosia.matsuokengo.com. Artosia is a free program for a church's media desk: it puts the words of songs, Bible verses and announcements on the projector during a service. It runs on Windows and Linux computers, and on Macs with Apple silicon once that edition is released; the page shows a system only when its download exists. The reader is a church volunteer of any age who was sent the link and wants to know what this is and how to get it. Register: informal and warm, addressing the reader the way a friendly program does in your language (kamu in Indonesian) where a pronoun is needed. Plain, modest, concrete: say what the thing is and does, then stop. No exclamation marks, no em-dash, no en-dash, no middle dot, no emoji. Sentence case. Program names (Artosia, EasiSlides, OpenLyrics, PowerPoint, Windows, Linux, Mac, macOS, GStreamer, Wi-Fi, GPL-3.0-or-later, artosia.exe) stay as written. Names of things inside the program must be the words the program itself uses in your language, the ones you chose for its window (Design, Screens, Announcements, Search, Prev and Next, the plan, Preview and Live).

meta_title.where: the browser tab and the search engine result's blue line
meta_title.does: names the program, then says in a few words what kind of program it is (free, for worship services, shows words on a projector, for Windows). Starts with 'Artosia:'

meta_description.where: the grey text under a search engine result
meta_description.does: one or two sentences: Artosia puts song words, Bible verses and announcements on a church's projector; it is free, for Windows and Linux, and the program itself speaks your language (name it) and nine others. Whole, natural grammar comes before shortness: a search engine cuts a long line at its end, so say what it is and the systems before the languages

meta_description_mac.where: the grey text under a search engine result, on the page that has a Mac download
meta_description_mac.does: the line above again with the Mac added: Artosia puts song words, Bible verses and announcements on a church's projector; it is free, for Windows, Linux and Mac, and the program itself speaks your language (name it) and nine others. Whole, natural grammar comes before shortness: a search engine cuts a long line at its end, so say what it is and the systems before the languages

nav_what.where: top bar link that jumps to the part of the page listing what the program does

nav_start.where: top bar link that jumps to the part where each system's download is
nav_start.does: names that part by the act of getting the program, one or two words

nav_language.where: top bar: what a screen reader says for the language menu. The menu shows this page's language in its own name and opens a list of the ten languages, each in its own name

nav_download.where: small button at the right of the top bar; pressing it downloads the program

hero_title.where: the big headline, the first thing read
hero_title.does: says what the program does in one short sentence ending in a full stop: the words of the songs appear on the projector screen. Must fit two lines on a phone

hero_lead.where: one sentence under the headline, grey
hero_lead.does: what Artosia is, in one plain sentence: free software, run from the media team's computer, that shows songs, scripture and announcements to a congregation through a projector; it names no operating system

source_button.where: quiet outline button beside the main one; opens the page where the program's source code is public
source_button.does: names what it opens: the source code

stage_prev.where: button under a picture of the program; steps the picture back one slide. It mirrors the program's own key for the previous slide
stage_prev.does: the program's own short word for going to the previous slide

stage_next.where: button under a picture of the program; steps the picture forward one slide. It mirrors the program's own key for the next slide
stage_next.does: the program's own short word for going to the next slide

stage_count.does: which picture of how many, using the tokens {n} and {of}, for example the Indonesian way of writing '2 of 4'. Keep both tokens exactly

stage_caption.where: one grey line beside the buttons, under the picture of the program's window
stage_caption.does: tells the reader to press the forward button (use the same word as stage_next), and that the row marked red is what the congregation sees on the projector

stage_alt_0.where: text read aloud by a screen reader in place of the first picture
stage_alt_0.does: describes it: the Artosia window, with the plan for the service on the left, the next song in the middle, and on the right the slide now on the projector, marked red

stage_alt_1.where: screen reader text for the second picture
stage_alt_1.does: the same window one slide later

stage_alt_2.where: screen reader text for the third picture
stage_alt_2.does: the same window two slides later

stage_alt_3.where: screen reader text for the fourth picture
stage_alt_3.does: the same window three slides later

what_title.where: heading of the part that shows what the program does, each with a picture
what_title.does: names the part, same idea as nav_what

wall_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the projector screen showing only four lines of a song
wall_title.does: the congregation sees nothing but the words

wall_text.does: the projector is run by a separate program of its own, so the words stay on the screen even if the operator's window stops working

wall_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
wall_caption.does: names what the picture is: the projector

wall_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
wall_alt.does: four lines of a song in white on a dark blue screen

search_title.where: small heading above a picture of the search box with songs found
search_title.does: a song can be found from any line of its words

search_text.where: one or two sentences under that heading
search_text.does: type the title or whatever line you remember; spelling mistakes are forgiven; the words that match are marked

search_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
search_caption.does: the search opens as soon as you start typing

search_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
search_alt.does: the search box with two words typed and four songs found, the matching words in blue

look_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the dialog where the look of the slides is chosen
look_title.does: you pick a look that is already made (you do not have to design one)

look_text.where: one or two sentences under that heading
look_text.does: six looks are ready; behind the words you can put a colour, a picture, a looping video or a camera; there are 318 free backgrounds to choose from

look_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
look_caption.does: the program's own Indonesian name for its Design dialog

look_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
look_alt.does: the Design dialog with six ready looks and a preview of the words

screens_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the dialog for projector screens, where four corners of the picture can be moved
screens_title.does: the crooked picture on the wall can be straightened without leaving the desk

screens_text.where: one or two sentences under that heading
screens_text.does: a second screen is found and filled automatically; you move its four corners until the picture on the wall is square

screens_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
screens_caption.does: the program's own Indonesian name for its Screens dialog

screens_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
screens_alt.does: the Screens dialog listing two screens, with four corners that can be moved

notices_title.where: small heading beside a picture of the announcements editor
notices_title.does: announcements shown before the service starts

notices_text.does: slides that repeat in a loop while people arrive; they can be typed in, or brought in from a PowerPoint file or from a list of birthdays

notices_caption.where: tiny grey label under that picture
notices_caption.does: the program's own Indonesian name for Announcements

notices_alt.where: screen reader text for that picture
notices_alt.does: the announcements editor: a list of slides, and a birthdays slide shown in the small projector preview

start_title.where: heading of the download part, above one row per system
start_title.does: the part where you obtain the program, as a short phrase with the program's name

zip_note.where: one sentence under the second download button, for the less common case; a link follows it
zip_note.does: for a computer that has no internet connection there is another way: a zip file of {zipsize} MB that you unpack into a folder of your own. Keep the token exactly

zip_link.where: a green text link right after that sentence; pressing it downloads the zip file
zip_link.does: the act: download the zip. It ends with a space and the arrow character →, as every action link on this site does

facts_title.where: heading of the last part, a list of short facts
facts_title.does: things worth knowing before you download

fact_runs_text.where: the fact under that label, on the page that has no Mac download yet
fact_runs_text.does: the systems it runs on, as three short facts: Windows versions 10 and 11 only, in their 64-bit form; Linux for ordinary 64-bit computers; the Mac edition does not exist yet

fact_runs_text_mac.where: the fact under that label, on the page that has a Mac download
fact_runs_text_mac.does: the systems it runs on, as one short list: Windows versions 10 and 11 only, in their 64-bit form; Linux for ordinary 64-bit computers; Macs with an Apple silicon chip (the Mac chip family, not Intel)

fact_needs_text.does: a projector or a second screen; one screen alone is enough to try the program

fact_bible_term.does: the Bible, the common Indonesian word

fact_bible_text.does: verses are called up by their reference, with an example reference written the Indonesian way (book Yohanes, chapter 3, verses 16 to 18, with a hyphen), taken from the Bibles you add to the program

fact_library_term.does: the song collection you already have from an older program

fact_library_text.does: it reads song files from EasiSlides and OpenLyrics

fact_phone_term.does: a phone, the everyday Indonesian word

fact_phone_text.does: a web page opened on a phone on the same Wi-Fi can move the slides

fact_language_text.does: the ten languages of the program's window, each named in your language, yours first: Indonesian, English, Chinese (simplified and traditional), Korean, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Vietnamese. A plain list, no sentence around it

fact_updates_text.does: every installed copy fetches the newest version by itself and checks its digital signature

fact_price_text.does: free; the source code is open under the licence GPL-3.0-or-later

footer_source.where: small footer link to the public source code

footer_releases.where: small footer link to the list of every released version

footer_licence.where: small footer link to the licence text

footer_privacy.where: small footer link to the privacy page, beside the licence link

version_line.where: small grey line under the download heading, above the rows
version_line.does: names the program version that every row below downloads: the word for version, then the token {version}. Keep the token exactly

os_windows.does: the operating system's own name as people write it in your language

os_linux.does: the operating system's own name as people write it in your language

os_mac.does: what people call Apple's computers in your language, as short as it can be

dl_windows.where: the filled black button of the Windows row, and the main hero button when the visitor uses Windows; pressing it downloads the setup
dl_windows.does: the act of downloading, and that it is for Windows

dl_linux.where: the link of the Linux row; it becomes the filled black button, also shown as the hero button, when the visitor uses Linux; pressing it downloads a package
dl_linux.does: the act of downloading, and that it is for Linux

dl_mac.where: the link of the Mac row; it becomes the filled black button, also shown as the hero button, when the visitor uses a Mac; pressing it downloads a disk image
dl_mac.does: the act of downloading, and that it is for Mac

win_file.where: small grey line under the Windows heading, repeated under the hero button when the visitor uses Windows
win_file.does: three facts separated by commas: the name of the file the button downloads, written exactly as Artosia-setup.exe; its size as the token {size} followed by MB; and the Windows versions it supports, 10 and 11. Keep the token exactly

win_do.where: one or two short sentences in the Windows row, above its button
win_do.does: what to do with the file: open it; and that the first time Windows may warn that it does not know the publisher

linux_file.where: small grey line under the Linux heading, repeated under the hero button when the visitor uses Linux
linux_file.does: two facts separated by a comma: the name of the file the link downloads, written exactly as Artosia-linux-x86_64.tar.gz; its size as the token {linuxsize} followed by MB. Keep the token exactly

linux_do.where: two short sentences in the Linux row, above its link
linux_do.does: how to start: unpack the downloaded archive into the user's home folder and run the program called artosia (written exactly so); then a warning that playing video needs the GStreamer library to be installed on the computer

mac_file.where: small grey line under the Mac heading, repeated under the hero button when the visitor uses a Mac
mac_file.does: three facts separated by commas: the name of the file the link downloads, written exactly as Artosia-macos-aarch64.dmg; its size as the token {macsize} followed by MB; and that it is for Apple silicon Macs. Keep the token exactly

mac_do.where: two short sentences in the Mac row, above its link
mac_do.does: how to install: open the downloaded disk image and drag Artosia onto the Applications folder shown beside it (the folder named as macOS names it in your language); after that Artosia is opened from Applications like any other program

also_linux.where: grey line under the hero buttons when the visitor uses Windows and the page has no Mac download
